name: Reproductive system
description: The male and female reproductive organs, sperm and eggs, the hormones behind the menstrual cycle, fertilisation and pregnancy. Picture questions show the male organs, drawn see-through inside the pelvis, with one part highlighted to name. BodyParts3D has no female organs, so those are text questions.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy. Pictures rendered from BodyParts3D (© The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP).

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT an organ of the male reproductive tract?
questions.explanation: The kidney belongs to the urinary system, though the male urethra carries both urine and semen.

figure.alt: The male reproductive organs inside the pelvis, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the male gonads called?
questions.explanation: They make sperm and testosterone.

questions.prompt: Which organs are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Oval glands about 4.5 cm long, hanging in the scrotum.

figure.alt: The male reproductive organs inside the pelvis, with one part in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Why do the testes hang outside the body in the scrotum?
answers: Sperm develop best a little below body temperature
It keeps them about 2 to 3 degrees cooler than the body
wrong: There is no room for them in the pelvis
To keep them warmer than the body
questions.explanation: The cremaster muscle and the pampiniform plexus of veins help to regulate the temperature.

figure.alt: The male reproductive organs inside the pelvis, with the testes in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Where inside the testis are sperm made?
questions.explanation: Several hundred tightly coiled tubules in each testis.

questions.prompt: Which cells between the seminiferous tubules make testosterone?
questions.explanation: Stimulated by luteinising hormone (LH).

questions.prompt: Which cells in the seminiferous tubules nourish the developing sperm and form the blood–testis barrier?
questions.explanation: Stimulated by follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).

questions.prompt: About how long does it take a sperm to develop from a spermatogonium?
questions.explanation: So the testes make millions of sperm every day, from puberty on.

questions.prompt: What are the three main parts of a sperm?
questions.explanation: The head holds the nucleus and acrosome with its enzymes; the midpiece is packed with mitochondria; the tail is a flagellum.

questions.prompt: What does the cap on the sperm's head, the acrosome, contain?
answers: Enzymes that help it penetrate the egg

questions.prompt: How many chromosomes does a sperm carry?
questions.explanation: Half the usual 46: it is haploid.

questions.prompt: Which structures are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A tightly coiled tube lying along the back of each testis, where sperm mature and are stored.

figure.alt: The testes and epididymides in the scrotum, with the epididymides in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What happens to sperm in the epididymis?
answers: They mature and gain the ability to swim
wrong: They are mixed with seminal fluid
questions.explanation: They spend about two weeks there.

figure.alt: The male reproductive organs inside the pelvis, with the epididymides in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which structures are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Each duct carries sperm from the epididymis up through the inguinal canal, over the bladder, to join the seminal vesicle.

figure.alt: The male reproductive organs inside the pelvis, with one part in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is cut or tied in a vasectomy?
questions.explanation: Semen is still made, but without sperm. The testes go on making testosterone.

questions.prompt: Which structure, running through the inguinal canal, holds the ductus deferens together with the testicular vessels and nerves?
Which glands are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Two glands behind the bladder that make about 60% of the volume of semen.

figure.alt: The male reproductive organs seen from behind, with the seminal vesicles in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which sugar in the secretion of the seminal vesicles gives sperm their energy?
questions.explanation: It also contains prostaglandins, which cause contractions in the female tract.

questions.prompt: Which gland is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A chestnut-sized gland just below the bladder, wrapped around the first part of the urethra.

figure.alt: The prostate seen from the side, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What does the prostate add to semen?
answers: A thin, milky, slightly acid fluid with enzymes and citrate
questions.explanation: About 30% of semen. It includes PSA, an enzyme that thins the semen after ejaculation.

figure.alt: The prostate seen from the side, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What condition makes the prostate enlarge in older men and hinders the flow of urine?
questions.explanation: Because it surrounds the urethra.

questions.prompt: What is PSA, a blood test used in screening men for prostate disease?
Which pair of small glands below the prostate releases a clear, slippery fluid before ejaculation?
questions.explanation: It neutralises the acid of urine left in the urethra.

questions.prompt: What is the path of sperm from the testis to the outside?
answers: Seminiferous tubules, epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory duct, urethra
Testis, epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory duct, urethra
wrong: Epididymis, seminiferous tubules, ductus deferens, urethra, ejaculatory duct
Seminiferous tubules, ductus deferens, epididymis, ejaculatory duct, urethra
Seminiferous tubules, epididymis, ureter, bladder, urethra
questions.explanation: The ejaculatory duct is formed by the ductus deferens and the duct of the seminal vesicle, and goes through the prostate.

questions.prompt: About how much semen is in a normal ejaculation?
questions.explanation: With roughly 20 to 150 million sperm per mL in a fertile man.

questions.prompt: Which three parts does the male urethra have, from the bladder down?
questions.explanation: The spongy urethra runs through the corpus spongiosum.

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The organ of urination and of delivering sperm.

figure.alt: The penis seen from the side, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which structure is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: One of a pair of columns of erectile tissue along the top of the shaft. They fill with blood in erection.

figure.alt: The shaft of the penis from the side, with the corpus cavernosum in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which column of erectile tissue, below the corpora cavernosa, surrounds the urethra and expands at the tip into the glans?
questions.explanation: It stays softer in an erection so that the urethra remains open.

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The cone-shaped head of the penis, covered in the foreskin (prepuce) unless circumcised.

figure.alt: The head of the penis from the side, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which division of the autonomic nervous system causes erection?
questions.explanation: It widens the arteries, which fill the erectile tissue with blood. Ejaculation is sympathetic.

questions.prompt: Which hormone, made mostly in the testes, drives male puberty and sperm production?
questions.explanation: Its secretion is controlled by LH from the anterior pituitary.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a testis that has not descended into the scrotum?
questions.explanation: Untreated, it harms fertility and raises the risk of testicular cancer.

questions.prompt: What are the female gonads called?
questions.explanation: They make eggs (ova) and the hormones oestrogen and progesterone.

questions.prompt: Which of these lists the internal organs of the female reproductive tract?
About how big is an ovary?
answers: About the size of an almond
wrong: About the size of a pea
About the size of an orange
About the size of a fist
questions.explanation: About 3 cm long, 2 cm wide and 1 cm thick, one on each side of the uterus.

questions.prompt: What is the small fluid-filled sac in the ovary that holds a developing egg called?
questions.explanation: A mature one is called a Graafian (or antral) follicle.

questions.prompt: What is the release of an egg from the ovary called?
questions.explanation: It happens about 14 days before the next period.

questions.prompt: What does the ruptured follicle become after ovulation, making progesterone?
questions.explanation: If there is no pregnancy it shrinks to a scar, the corpus albicans.

questions.prompt: When does a female make all of her primary oocytes?
questions.explanation: About one to two million at birth, and about 400 are ever ovulated.

questions.prompt: What are the finger-like edges at the end of the uterine tube that sweep the egg in?
Where does fertilisation normally happen?
answers: In the ampulla of the uterine tube
questions.explanation: Within about 24 hours of ovulation.

questions.prompt: What is a pregnancy that implants outside the uterus, most often in the uterine tube, called?
questions.explanation: It can rupture and cause life-threatening bleeding.

questions.prompt: About what shape and size is the uterus in a woman who has not been pregnant?
wrong: About the size of a football
questions.explanation: It lies between the bladder in front and the rectum behind.

questions.prompt: What are the three layers of the uterine wall, from inside out?
questions.explanation: The functional layer of the endometrium is shed in menstruation. The myometrium is smooth muscle that contracts in labour.

questions.prompt: What are the three parts of the uterus, from top to bottom?
What is the narrow lower end of the uterus, which projects into the vagina, called?
questions.explanation: Its mucus changes through the cycle. A smear test samples its cells.

questions.prompt: Which organ is a muscular tube about 8 to 10 cm long, from the cervix to the outside, which is also the birth canal?
questions.explanation: Its lining is acidic, which protects against infection.

questions.prompt: What is the name for the female external genitalia as a whole?
questions.explanation: It includes the labia majora and minora, the clitoris and the vestibule.

questions.prompt: Which structure of the vulva is made of erectile tissue and is the female equivalent of the penis?
Which sheet of peritoneum holds the uterus, uterine tubes and ovaries in place?
Which hormone, made mostly by the ovarian follicles, builds up the endometrium and brings on the female body changes of puberty?
questions.explanation: After ovulation, progesterone from the corpus luteum prepares the lining for implantation.

questions.prompt: Which hormone, made by the corpus luteum, keeps the endometrium ready for a pregnancy?
Which hormone makes the breasts produce milk?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin makes the milk let down, by contracting the cells around the ducts.

questions.prompt: At about what age do the periods stop (menopause) in women?
questions.explanation: The ovaries run out of follicles, so oestrogen falls.

questions.prompt: How long is the average menstrual cycle?
questions.explanation: Counted from the first day of one period to the first day of the next. It varies from 21 to 35 days.

questions.prompt: What are the phases of the menstrual cycle, in order, starting with the period?
answers: Menstruation, follicular phase, ovulation, luteal phase
questions.explanation: The follicular phase is when the endometrium rebuilds. The luteal phase is when it is prepared for implantation.

questions.prompt: Which hormone surge triggers ovulation?
questions.explanation: Made by the anterior pituitary, and set off by a rise in oestrogen.

questions.prompt: Which pituitary hormone makes ovarian follicles grow in women and supports sperm production in men?
Which hormone from the hypothalamus tells the pituitary to release LH and FSH?
What causes menstruation?
answers: A fall in progesterone and oestrogen when no pregnancy has started
The corpus luteum breaks down, so hormone levels fall
questions.explanation: The functional layer of the endometrium is shed over about 5 days.

questions.prompt: What is the cell formed when a sperm fertilises an egg called?
questions.explanation: It has 46 chromosomes.

questions.prompt: In order, what are the early stages of the developing embryo, from the zygote?
questions.explanation: The blastocyst implants in the endometrium about 6 to 7 days after fertilisation.

questions.prompt: About how long after fertilisation does the embryo implant in the uterine wall?
Which hormone, made by the developing placenta, is what pregnancy tests detect?
questions.explanation: It keeps the corpus luteum making progesterone in early pregnancy.

questions.prompt: Which organ lets oxygen and nutrients pass from the mother to the fetus, and wastes the other way?
questions.explanation: The two bloods do not mix. It also makes hormones.

questions.prompt: How many vessels does the umbilical cord have?
answers: Three: two arteries and one vein
wrong: Two: one artery and one vein
Three: two veins and one artery
questions.explanation: The vein carries oxygenated blood to the fetus; the arteries carry deoxygenated blood away.

questions.prompt: About how long is a human pregnancy, from the last period?
questions.explanation: About 38 weeks from fertilisation.

questions.prompt: How long is each trimester of pregnancy?
questions.explanation: The organs are formed in the first trimester, which is the time of greatest risk from drugs and infection.

questions.prompt: Which hormone from the posterior pituitary makes the uterus contract in labour?
questions.explanation: It is also behind the milk let-down reflex.

questions.prompt: What type of cell division makes eggs and sperm, with half the chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Each cell ends with 23 chromosomes. Fertilisation restores 46.

questions.prompt: Which sex chromosomes does a typical female have, and a typical male?
answers: XX in females, XY in males
questions.explanation: The sex of the child is set by whether the sperm carries an X or a Y.

questions.prompt: Which method of birth control blocks the uterine tubes?
questions.explanation: Vasectomy is the male counterpart.

tests.why: Pictures of the male reproductive organs, each with one part in red to name.

tests.why: Type each answer from memory, starting with the ones due for review. Small typos are forgiven.
